[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
William is reported to have been born in 1760. He is attached as the son of [[Glasgow-2916|James Glasgow]] and husband of Margaret Mitchell, but no inspected contemporary record currently proves either relationship or a Cookstown identity.

== Research Notes ==
=== Cross and Cookstown evidence gap ===

PRONI's official church-register guide lists Derryloran Church of Ireland baptisms only from 1795/1797. The listed Presbyterian baptism registers at Cookstown begin in 1822, 1835 or 1836.<ref>[https://www.proni.gov.uk/publications/proni-guide-church-records Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, ''Guide to Church Records''], Derryloran CR1/114 and MIC1/15/1; First Cookstown Presbyterian MIC1P/43, MIC1P/139 and MIC1P/460; guide consulted 30 August 2026.</ref> Those surviving series are too late to record a birth about 1760. Exact-name searches completed on 30 August 2026 located no primary record tying William to Margaret Mitchell or to the attached father.

This register gap does not disprove the family. It means the present chain should remain a research hypothesis while deeds, estate papers, probate, religious returns and migration records are sought. No attached person or location should be changed without positive replacement evidence.

=== Kildress delegate candidate, 1793 ===

The Northern Star report of a meeting at Kildress church on 16 January 1793 names William Glasgow and Hugh Faulkner as delegates to the Dungannon meeting on parliamentary reform. William subsequently took the chair and signed the thanks resolution.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/72019090/ Northern Star, 23 January 1793, p.2].</ref> The reported birth about 1760 and Cookstown association make this a compatible identity candidate, but the notice states no age, wife, father or precise residence. It does not establish either attached relationship.

=== Further publication of the Kildress resolutions, 1793 ===

A further issue repeats the Kildress resolutions naming Hugh Faulkner and William Glasgow as delegates and Glasgow taking the chair. The meeting date is 16 January 1793, established by the complete headed account; the 30 January issue date is a publication date, not another meeting. No spouse, parent or birthplace is stated.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/72019090/ Northern Star, 23 January 1793, p.2].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/72019250/ Northern Star, 26 January 1793, p.4, repeated Kildress resolutions].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/72019314/ Northern Star, 1793-01-30, p.4].</ref>

The repeated publication supplies no new family relationship. The reported c.1760 birth and Cookstown association support a compatible delegate identification, but the notice proves neither his attached father nor spouse.
